title: Red 40
plain: Red 40 is a bright dye the FDA allows in food. Some families choose to limit artificial colors. This is not a claim about any brand.

title: Yellow 5
plain: Yellow 5 is an artificial color the FDA allows. The label has to list it. Some people choose to limit it.

title: Yellow 6
plain: Yellow 6 is an artificial color the FDA allows in food. Some shoppers prefer to limit dyes like this.

title: Blue 1
plain: Blue 1 is an artificial color the FDA allows. It is a dye, not a fruit or vegetable color.

title: Blue 2
plain: Blue 2 is an artificial color the FDA allows in foods such as candy and drinks.

title: Green 3
plain: Green 3 is an artificial color the FDA allows. It is not the same as green from vegetables.

title: Red 3
plain: Red 3 is an artificial color. The FDA has tightened where it can be used. Many shoppers choose foods without it.

title: Caramel color
plain: Caramel color is a brown coloring the FDA allows. It is added for color, not as cooked sugar from a home kitchen.

title: Annatto
plain: Annatto is a plant color found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Beta carotene
plain: Beta carotene is a plant color that the body can turn into vitamin A found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Turmeric
plain: Turmeric is a plant color and spice found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Beet color
plain: Beet color is a color from beets found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Paprika extract
plain: Paprika extract is a color from peppers found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Titanium dioxide
plain: Titanium dioxide is a white coloring. The FDA still allows it. The European Union no longer allows it in food. That is a difference in rules, not a verdict on a brand.

title: Carmine
plain: Carmine is a red color made from insects. The FDA allows it, and the label should say so. It is not a plant color, and it is not vegan.

title: Aspartame
plain: Aspartame is a low-calorie sweetener the FDA allows within a daily limit. People with phenylketonuria need to avoid it. This is general information, not medical advice.

title: Sucralose
plain: Sucralose is a low-calorie sweetener the FDA allows. It is much sweeter than sugar, so foods use a tiny amount.

title: Acesulfame potassium
plain: Acesulfame potassium is a low-calorie sweetener the FDA allows. It is often paired with other sweeteners.

title: Saccharin
plain: Saccharin is a low-calorie sweetener the FDA allows. It has been used for many years.

title: Stevia
plain: Stevia is a sweetener from the stevia plant found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Monk fruit
plain: Monk fruit is a sweetener from monk fruit found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Sorbitol
plain: Sorbitol is a sugar alcohol used in sugar-free foods. Large amounts can bother some people's stomachs. This is not medical advice.

title: Mannitol
plain: Mannitol is a sugar alcohol. Large amounts can bother some people's stomachs. Labels on some foods say so.

title: Xylitol
plain: Xylitol is a sugar alcohol used in sugar-free gum and mints found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Erythritol
plain: Erythritol is a sugar alcohol the FDA allows. Research about it is still mixed. This note is not a warning about a brand and not medical advice.

title: Maltitol
plain: Maltitol is a sugar alcohol. It still has some calories, and a large amount can bother some stomachs.

title: High-fructose corn syrup
plain: High-fructose corn syrup is a sweetener made from corn. It counts as added sugar. A high amount per serving lowers the score.

title: Corn syrup
plain: Corn syrup is a sugar syrup from corn. It counts toward added sugar when it is used to sweeten a food.

title: Dextrose
plain: Dextrose is a simple sugar found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Sugar
plain: Sugar is a sweetener. Added sugar per serving is counted in the score found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Honey
plain: Honey is a sweetener made by bees. It still counts as added sugar when used that way found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Molasses
plain: Molasses is a thick sweetener from sugar cane found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Agave
plain: Agave is a plant syrup used as a sweetener. It still counts as added sugar.

title: Invert sugar
plain: Invert sugar is a liquid form of sugar found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Maltodextrin
plain: Maltodextrin is a processed starch used to thicken or carry flavors. It is allowed in food.

title: Neotame
plain: Neotame is a low-calorie sweetener the FDA allows in very small amounts.

title: Advantame
plain: Advantame is a low-calorie sweetener the FDA allows in very small amounts.

title: Cyclamate
plain: Cyclamate is not approved as a sweetener in U.S. food. If a label lists it, that is worth a closer look.

title: Sodium nitrite
plain: Sodium nitrite is used to cure meats such as bacon and hot dogs. The FDA sets limits. Health agencies suggest keeping processed meats modest. This is not medical advice.

title: Sodium nitrate
plain: Sodium nitrate is used in some cured meats. The FDA sets limits for it.

title: Potassium nitrite
plain: Potassium nitrite is a curing salt used in some meats, with FDA limits.

title: BHA
plain: BHA is a preservative that helps fats stay fresh. The FDA allows it. Some shoppers choose to limit it.

title: BHT
plain: BHT is a preservative that helps fats stay fresh. The FDA allows it. Some shoppers choose to limit it.

title: TBHQ
plain: TBHQ is a preservative used to keep fats from going stale. The FDA allows a limited amount.

title: Sodium benzoate
plain: Sodium benzoate is a preservative the FDA allows. It slows spoilage in acidic foods such as soda and dressings.

title: Potassium sorbate
plain: Potassium sorbate is a preservative that slows mold found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Calcium propionate
plain: Calcium propionate is a preservative that slows mold in bread found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Sorbic acid
plain: Sorbic acid is a preservative that slows mold found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Sulfites
plain: Sulfites keep some foods from browning. The FDA requires a label when they are used at higher levels because some people are sensitive. This is not medical advice.

title: Sodium metabisulfite
plain: Sodium metabisulfite is a sulfite preservative. Some people are sensitive to sulfites.

title: Potassium metabisulfite
plain: Potassium metabisulfite is a sulfite preservative. Some people are sensitive to sulfites.

title: Natamycin
plain: Natamycin is a preservative used on the surface of some cheeses found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Ascorbic acid
plain: Ascorbic acid is vitamin C, often used to keep color found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Sodium erythorbate
plain: Sodium erythorbate is a form of vitamin C used to keep color in cured meat found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Citric acid
plain: Citric acid is an acid found in citrus, used for tartness and freshness found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Sodium citrate
plain: Sodium citrate is a salt of citric acid, used to manage tartness found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Lactic acid
plain: Lactic acid is an acid found in fermented foods found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Acetic acid
plain: Acetic acid is the acid in vinegar found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Malic acid
plain: Malic acid is an acid found in apples, used for tartness found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Phosphoric acid
plain: Phosphoric acid adds tartness, especially in colas. It is allowed. It is not a fruit.

title: Sodium phosphate
plain: Sodium phosphate is a mineral salt used to keep texture found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Tocopherols
plain: Tocopherols is vitamin E, often used to keep oils fresh found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Rosemary extract
plain: Rosemary extract is an herb extract used to keep fats fresh found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Propyl gallate
plain: Propyl gallate is a preservative for fats. The FDA allows a limited amount.

title: EDTA
plain: EDTA is a preservative that binds minerals so food keeps its color found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Cultured celery powder
plain: Celery powder is often used in meats labeled uncured. It can still supply nitrite. Read it as a curing ingredient, not as a vegetable serving.

title: Partially hydrogenated oil
plain: Partially hydrogenated oils are the main source of industrial trans fat. The FDA removed them from the U.S. food supply. If a label still lists them, that is worth avoiding.

title: Hydrogenated oil
plain: Fully hydrogenated oil is not the same as partially hydrogenated oil. It is still a processed fat. Check which words the label uses.

title: Palm oil
plain: Palm oil is a common cooking fat. It is higher in saturated fat than many liquid oils. Saturated fat is counted in the score.

title: Canola oil
plain: Canola oil is a liquid cooking oil found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Olive oil
plain: Olive oil is an oil pressed from olives found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Sunflower oil
plain: Sunflower oil is a liquid oil from sunflower seeds found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Soybean oil
plain: Soybean oil is a common liquid cooking oil. It is a soy ingredient found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Corn oil
plain: Corn oil is a liquid oil from corn found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Coconut oil
plain: Coconut oil is a plant oil that is high in saturated fat. Saturated fat is counted in the score.

title: Palm kernel oil
plain: Palm kernel oil is high in saturated fat. Saturated fat is counted in the score.

title: Mono and diglycerides
plain: Mono and diglycerides is fats used to blend oil and water found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Polysorbate 80
plain: Polysorbate 80 helps oil and water stay mixed. The FDA allows it in set amounts.

title: Lecithin
plain: Lecithin is an emulsifier, often from soy or sunflower found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: DATEM
plain: DATEM is a dough strengthener used in some breads found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Sodium stearoyl lactylate
plain: Sodium stearoyl lactylate is a dough conditioner used in some breads found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Interesterified fat
plain: Interesterified fat is a processed fat used to change texture. It is not the same as partially hydrogenated oil.

title: Carrageenan
plain: Carrageenan is a thickener made from seaweed. It is allowed in food. Some people prefer to limit it. Research opinions differ, and this is not a verdict on a brand.

title: Xanthan gum
plain: Xanthan gum is a thickener made by fermentation found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Guar gum
plain: Guar gum is a thickener from guar beans found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Locust bean gum
plain: Locust bean gum is a thickener from carob seeds found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Gellan gum
plain: Gellan gum is a thickener made by fermentation found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Cellulose
plain: Cellulose is plant fiber used to add bulk or prevent caking found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Cellulose gum
plain: Cellulose gum is a thickener made from plant fiber that has been processed. It is allowed in food.

title: Modified food starch
plain: Modified food starch is starch treated so it thickens more evenly found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Pectin
plain: Pectin is a fiber from fruit, used to thicken jams found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Gelatin
plain: Gelatin is a protein from animal collagen. It is not vegan found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Agar
plain: Agar is a thickener from seaweed found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Sodium alginate
plain: Sodium alginate is a thickener from seaweed found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Silicon dioxide
plain: Silicon dioxide is a mineral that keeps powders from clumping found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Gum arabic
plain: Gum arabic is a thickener from the acacia tree found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Tara gum
plain: Tara gum is a thickener from tara seeds found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Propylene glycol alginate
plain: Propylene glycol alginate is a thickener from seaweed, used in dressings found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Monosodium glutamate
plain: Monosodium glutamate is a flavor enhancer. The FDA treats it as safe. A few people say they feel unwell after large amounts. This is not medical advice found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Disodium inosinate
plain: Disodium inosinate is a flavor helper often used with monosodium glutamate found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Disodium guanylate
plain: Disodium guanylate is a flavor helper often used with monosodium glutamate found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Yeast extract
plain: Yeast extract is a savory flavor from yeast found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Natural flavors
plain: Natural flavors is flavors from plants or animals. The word natural does not mean the whole food is unprocessed found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Artificial flavors
plain: Artificial flavors are made to taste like a food. They are allowed. They are not the food itself.

title: Smoke flavor
plain: Smoke flavor is a flavor that tastes like smoke found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Hydrolyzed protein
plain: Hydrolyzed protein is a savory ingredient made by breaking a protein apart. The source, such as soy or corn, matters for allergies.

title: Caffeine
plain: Caffeine is a stimulant. It is allowed in foods and drinks. Many people limit how much they have, especially for kids and during pregnancy. This is not medical advice.

title: Potassium bromate
plain: Potassium bromate is a dough conditioner. Many countries do not allow it. Some U.S. bakers have stopped using it. If you see it, many shoppers skip that bread.

title: Azodicarbonamide
plain: Azodicarbonamide is a dough conditioner the FDA allows. It is not allowed in bread in the European Union.

title: Brominated vegetable oil
plain: The FDA no longer allows brominated vegetable oil in food. If an older label still lists it, skip that drink.

title: Calcium chloride
plain: Calcium chloride is a mineral salt used in cheese and canned vegetables found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Potassium chloride
plain: Potassium chloride is a salt substitute. It is not the same as table salt found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Baking soda
plain: Baking soda is a leavening ingredient found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Baking powder
plain: Baking powder is a leavening mix used in baked foods found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Calcium carbonate
plain: Calcium carbonate is a calcium mineral, also used as a white color found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Salt
plain: Salt is sodium chloride. A high amount of sodium per serving lowers the score found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Glycerin
plain: Glycerin is a sweet thick liquid used to keep foods soft found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Propylene glycol
plain: Propylene glycol keeps some foods moist and carries flavors. The FDA allows a limited amount in food. It is not the antifreeze chemical ethylene glycol.

title: Carnauba wax
plain: Carnauba wax is a plant wax used to shine some candies and fruit found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Beeswax
plain: Beeswax is a wax from bees, used to shine some foods. It is not vegan found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Shellac
plain: Shellac is a glaze from an insect resin, used to shine candy. It is allowed. It is not vegan.

title: Polydextrose
plain: Polydextrose is a processed fiber used to add bulk with fewer calories found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Inulin
plain: Inulin is a fiber from chicory or other plants found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Whey
plain: Whey is a protein from milk found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Casein
plain: Casein is a protein from milk found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Soy protein isolate
plain: Soy protein isolate is protein taken out of soybeans and dried. It is a processed soy ingredient.

title: Pea protein
plain: Pea protein is protein from peas found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Wheat gluten
plain: Wheat gluten is the protein in wheat. It matters if you avoid wheat found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Corn starch
plain: Corn starch is a starch from corn, used to thicken found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Rice starch
plain: Rice starch is a starch from rice found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Tapioca starch
plain: Tapioca starch is a starch from cassava found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Potato starch
plain: Potato starch is a starch from potatoes found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Niacin
plain: Niacin is a B vitamin often added to flour and cereal found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Riboflavin
plain: Riboflavin is a B vitamin, also used as a yellow color found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Thiamin
plain: Thiamin is a B vitamin often added to flour found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Vitamin B6
plain: Vitamin B6 is a B vitamin found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Vitamin B12
plain: Vitamin B12 is a B vitamin found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Vitamin D
plain: Vitamin D is a vitamin often added to milk and cereal found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Vitamin A
plain: Vitamin A is a vitamin. Very high amounts from supplements are a separate question for a clinician found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Folic acid
plain: Folic acid is a B vitamin added to many grain foods found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Iron
plain: Iron is a mineral often added to cereal and flour found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Zinc
plain: Zinc is a mineral sometimes added to food found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Calcium sulfate
plain: Calcium sulfate is a calcium mineral used in some baked foods and tofu found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Sodium aluminum phosphate
plain: Sodium aluminum phosphate helps baked foods rise. It is allowed. Some shoppers limit extra aluminum ingredients.

title: Calcium peroxide
plain: Calcium peroxide is a dough conditioner the FDA allows found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Benzoyl peroxide
plain: Benzoyl peroxide is used to bleach some flour. The FDA allows it for that use.

title: Trisodium phosphate
plain: Trisodium phosphate is a processing salt used to manage tartness and texture. It is allowed in food.

title: Sodium hydroxide
plain: Sodium hydroxide is a processing aid used, for example, to soften olives. It is not present as a household chemical in the finished food found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Olestra
plain: Olestra is a fat substitute the FDA allows in some snacks. It can bother some people's stomachs.

title: Transglutaminase
plain: Transglutaminase is an enzyme used to bind pieces of protein, sometimes called meat glue found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Allulose
plain: Allulose is a low-calorie sugar found in small amounts in some fruit found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Isomalt and lactitol
plain: Isomalt and lactitol is sugar alcohols used in sugar-free sweets found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Artificial vanilla
plain: Vanillin is a vanilla flavor that can be made in a factory. It is allowed. It is not the same as a vanilla bean.

title: Oat fiber
plain: Oat fiber is fiber from oats found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Sunflower lecithin
plain: Sunflower lecithin is an emulsifier from sunflower seeds found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Cottonseed oil
plain: Cottonseed oil is a common cooking oil in packaged food. It is a processed seed oil.

title: Safflower oil
plain: Safflower oil is a liquid oil from safflower seeds found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Bacterial cultures
plain: Bacterial cultures is helpful bacteria used to make yogurt and cheese found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Enzymes
plain: Enzymes is helpers used to make cheese, bread, and juice found in everyday food. U.S. rules allow it. This is general information, not a rating of a brand.

title: Trans fat
plain: Trans fat from partially hydrogenated oils is something the FDA moved out of the U.S. food supply. A line that still lists trans fat is worth avoiding.
